info.title: SlotFlow API
info.description:
Appointment booking for small service businesses.

**Every request needs a workspace.** Send an `X-Tenant: <slug>` header,
or authenticate — a token carries its own workspace and takes
precedence.

**Times are UTC on the wire.** Send ISO-8601 instants with an offset;
`2026-09-01T09:00:00+02:00` and `2026-09-01T07:00:00Z` describe the same
moment and are stored identically. Endpoints that render times for a
human take a required `tz` parameter — an IANA identifier such as
`Europe/Vienna`. Offsets and abbreviations are rejected, because
neither can express daylight saving.

**Money is integer minor units** plus a currency code. Never a float,
never pre-formatted.

**Errors share one shape**, whatever went wrong:

```json
{ "error": { "code": "slot_unavailable", "message": "…", "context": {} } }
```

Branch on `error.code`; it is the stable part of the contract. `409
slot_unavailable` in particular is a normal outcome on a busy diary,
not a failure — refresh availability and offer another time.

get.description:
Filter by `status`, `staff_id`, `service_id`, `risk`, and a `from`/`to`
date range. Results are paginated.

get.description:
The stored settings, what is actually in force after platform fallback,
and the models available to choose from.

put.description: Both accept null, meaning "use the platform default".

The key is checked against the Anthropic API first. If the check fails
nothing is written and the response explains why, so a bad paste is a
message rather than a silently broken workspace.

delete.description:
Model and budget preferences survive, so putting a key back later does
not mean reconfiguring everything else. AI features keep working —
they fall back to the platform key if one exists, and to the built-in
implementations if not.

post.description:
A key that verified when it was saved can be revoked later. This is how
an owner finds that out on purpose, rather than by noticing the AI has
gone quiet.

message.const: This workspace has no key of its own to check.

post.description:
Creates a customer account in the workspace named by the `X-Tenant`
header, and returns a token.
Exchanges credentials for a bearer token.
Revokes only the token used for this request; other devices stay signed in.

get.description:
`tz` is required and every returned slot carries both the UTC instant
and its rendering in that zone. Slots are grouped by local date, which
is what a calendar UI needs and what a date boundary in the caller's
zone actually means.

parameters.name: tz
parameters.description:
Required, not optional with a default. A booking API that
guesses the caller's timezone is a booking API that is
occasionally an hour wrong, and never says so.

cache_ttl_seconds.description:
Told, not implied. A client that caches responses needs to
know the server already did, and for how long.

put.description:
Send the complete week. The operation is a replace, not a merge, so it
is idempotent — sending the same payload twice leaves the same schedule.

post.description:
Returns 409 `slot_unavailable` if the slot went between the customer
seeing it and confirming it — the normal race, not an error condition.
Retry against fresh availability.

path.description: Base path for paginator generated URLs.

per_page.description: Number of items shown per page.

to.description: Number of the last item in the slice.

total.description: Total number of items being paginated.

get.description:
Looked up by reference (e.g. `BL-7Q4M2X`). A guest may read their own
booking by also passing the email it was made with — enough to be
useful in a confirmation link, not enough to enumerate.

post.description:
Send what the customer typed. The response contains the parsed intent,
the matched service and up to `limit` slots that are genuinely free —
they come from the availability engine, not from the model.

Booking one still requires `POST /bookings`. This endpoint never writes.

The `ai` object reports which driver answered (`claude` or `heuristic`)
and why, if it degraded. Show that to the user rather than hiding it.

message.const: That service is not available for online booking. Please pick one from the list.

get.description:
The figures in `stats` are computed by the application. The model only
decides which of them matter and writes the sentences.

Bookings, revenue and the no-show rate over a rolling window, plus
today's schedule statistics.

lost_to_no_shows_cents.description:
What the no-shows cost. This is the number the whole
risk feature exists to move, so it belongs on the
dashboard next to it.

get.description:
Every AI call this workspace has made, aggregated by task. What it cost,
how long it took, how often it fell back.

The score and factors are deterministic — the same booking always scores
the same. Only `rationale` and `recommended_action` are model-written,
and `generated_by` says which of the two produced them.

Pass `refresh=1` to recompute (the customer's history may have moved).
Returns active services by default. Owners may pass `include_inactive=1`.

delete.description:
Refuses while future bookings exist. Deactivate it instead — deleting a
service that people are booked into would orphan their appointments.

post.description:
Returns a draft for a human to edit. It is not saved anywhere — the
owner still has to accept it in the form.

get.description: Filter to those who perform one service with `service_id`.

delete.description: Refuses while future bookings exist, for the same reason as services.

post.description:
Existing bookings inside the interval are *not* cancelled automatically.
Silently dropping appointments someone has already promised to attend is
not a decision an API should make; the conflicts are returned instead so
the caller can deal with them.

starts_at.description:
Wall-clock times, trimmed to HH:MM. The staff timezone they
belong to travels with the staff member, not with each rule.

text.description:
Capped at 400 characters: this is a booking request, not a
conversation. A cap is also the cheapest defence against
someone using an unauthenticated endpoint as free inference.

device_name.description:
Named so the owner can revoke one client without logging out
every other. Sanctum tokens are cheap; anonymous ones are not.

factors.description:
The full arithmetic ships with the score. A client that wants to
show only the number can ignore it; a client that wants to
justify a deposit request cannot get it any other way.

price_cents.description:
Minor units and the currency code, never a pre-formatted string.
Formatting money is the client's job; it knows the locale.

api_key.description:
No prefix rule. `starts_with:sk-ant-` would catch a pasted Stripe key without a
network round trip, and would also reject a perfectly good key
the day Anthropic changes its format. The API is the authority
on whether a credential works, and it is consulted before
anything is stored — so a wrong key fails with a clear message
either way, and a valid one is never refused by a guess about
its shape.

model.description:
Restricted to models we can price. Allowing anything else means
cost tracking silently reports zero, which is worse than
refusing the model.

starts_at.description:
ISO-8601 with an offset. "2026-09-01T09:00:00+02:00" and
"2026-09-01T07:00:00Z" are the same booking and are stored
identically; a bare "2026-09-01 09:00" is ambiguous and rejected.

SyncAvailabilityRulesRequest.description:
Replaces a staff member's whole weekly pattern in one call.

A PUT of the complete set rather than per-row POST/DELETE, because a week's
hours are edited as a unit. It also makes the operation idempotent: the same
payload sent twice leaves the same schedule.
SyncAvailabilityRulesRequest.title: SyncAvailabilityRulesRequest

monthly_budget_usd.description:
Null means "use the platform default". Zero means "no ceiling",
which is a decision an owner is allowed to make explicitly but
will never arrive at by accident.

errors.description: A detailed description of each field that failed validation.
